settings.title: Settings
settings.auto_start_hint: Off by default. WireGuide Plus's background helper runs only while the app is open — automation rules apply during that time. Turn this on to have WireGuide Plus start with your session.
settings.start_minimized_hint: When enabled, the app starts minimized — on Windows to the taskbar (the taskbar button stays visible so you can always reopen the window), on macOS/Linux to the system tray.
settings.notify_duration_hint: How long the connection-status bubble stays on screen; it can also be dismissed manually.
settings.compact_list_hint: Denser rows — hides the endpoint line and shrinks row height so more tunnels fit without scrolling.
settings.kill_switch_hint: Blocks all traffic if VPN drops. Applied automatically on connect.
settings.dns_protection_hint: Forces DNS through VPN only. Applied automatically on connect.
settings.health_check_hint: Monitors handshake age and triggers reconnect if tunnel is dead for 180s. Recommended with PersistentKeepalive.
settings.pin_interface_hint: Pins VPN bypass routes to the active network interface. Prevents latency spikes when WiFi and Ethernet are both connected.
settings.about_desc: An open-source VPN client built around WireGuard — drop a config and you're online. A kill switch that doesn't leak, DNS protection that doesn't dodge, and Wi-Fi rules that pick the right tunnel on networks you trust. No command line. No telemetry. No upsell.
settings.about_credits: Built with WireGuard®, Wails, and Svelte.
settings.about_fork_thanks: v0.5.1 — with thanks to the original author.
settings.auto_update_check_hint: When on, WireGuide Plus checks GitHub once a day (with jitter and conditional GETs so it never wastes the public API quota).
settings.legacy_migration_hint: Data left by pre-rename installs (stored under "wireguide"). Re-runs the startup migration dialog.
settings.proxy_hint: Network access for update checks and update downloads. If GitHub is unreachable directly, use an accelerator mirror or a local HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy.
settings.proxy_mirror_hint: No local proxy software needed — rewrite GitHub API requests through a public accelerator, e.g. https://ghfast.top
settings.proxy_manual_hint: Tunnel through proxy software running locally (e.g. Clash), e.g. http://127.0.0.1:7890
settings.log_retention_hint: Daily log files older than this are deleted automatically (files are written to the log folder one per day).
settings.history_retention_hint: Connection history older than this is pruned automatically. The list is also always capped at 200 records.
settings.log_folder_hint: The folder where GUI and helper daily log files are stored.
settings.tunnels_folder_hint: The folder where your WireGuard config files live.
settings.wg_scripts_hint: Execute PreUp/PostUp/PreDown/PostDown commands from your tunnel configs, like wg-quick. Off by default — scripts run inside the privileged helper.
settings.wg_scripts_warn: Enabling this runs arbitrary commands from your tunnel configs as the system administrator (root). Only enable it for configs you fully trust — a malicious config could change or delete anything on this computer.
settings.enable_awg_hint: Allows tunnels that use AmneziaWG (AWG) obfuscation to connect. AWG is a WireGuard fork with traffic obfuscation. Turn this off only if the AWG backend misbehaves on this machine — AWG tunnels won't connect while it is off.

tools.dns_leak_desc: Verifies that your DNS queries go through the VPN tunnel, not your ISP. A leak means websites you visit could be visible to your ISP even with VPN active.
tools.dns_browser_title: Run a real-browser DNS & WebRTC leak test via browserleaks.com (opens your default browser)
tools.dns_browser_hint: The local test above inspects your system DNS configuration. A browser-level test observes where real browser DNS queries land (plus WebRTC leaks) and is sent to a third-party site.
tools.dns_public_section_desc: Besides your system-configured DNS, the test also sends queries to the public resolvers below as a cross-check (a reply only proves reachability — it is not a leak). Edit, delete, or add entries freely; clearing the list restores the default cross-check set — public probing always stays on. Use "Fetch from network" to refresh the default list from public-dns.info.
tools.dns_public_add_placeholder: Enter an IP or hostname, then press Enter
tools.dns_public_none: No custom public resolvers — the default cross-check list is in use. Clearing the list never disables public probing.
tools.dns_public_refresh_title: Fetch the latest public DNS list from public-dns.info
tools.dns_public_fetch_timeout: Network timeout — public-dns.info is too slow or unreachable. The previous list is still in effect.
tools.dns_server_note: "Local" resolvers come from your physical network adapters (WLAN/Ethernet, the same list as ipconfig /all) and are shown first; "VPN" resolvers are the tunnel's own DNS. The rest are well-known public resolvers probed as a cross-check. "In use" marks the server that actually answered the test query. A public resolver showing "OK" only means it is reachable — not a leak. The encryption badge shows the transport it offers: plaintext UDP/53 is normal but visible to anyone on the path; DoT (TCP/853) and DoH (TCP/443) encrypt your queries.
tools.dns_explain_leaked: Some DNS servers were reachable outside the tunnel, so your DNS queries are leaking to your ISP or local network — they can see which domains you resolve even while the VPN is connected.
tools.dns_explain_safe: Every detected DNS server answered only through the VPN, so your DNS queries are being routed through the tunnel. Your ISP cannot see which domains you resolve.
tools.dns_prevent_1: Use your VPN provider's DNS: set it in the tunnel config (DNS = ...) and, if the app offers it, enable DNS protection.
tools.dns_prevent_2: Prefer encrypted DNS (DoH or DoT) so queries stay private even if they leave the tunnel.
tools.dns_prevent_3: Use full-tunnel mode (AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0) so no DNS request can escape through the physical interface.
tools.dns_prevent_4: Turn off system features that override your VPN DNS, such as DHCP-supplied DNS on the physical adapter.
tools.route_desc: Shows where your network traffic is going. Routes marked VPN flow through the tunnel; others go directly to the internet.

wifi_permission.desc: Wi-Fi auto-connect rules need access to your current network name. Grant permission in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services.

automation.title: Automation
automation.hint: Rules run top to bottom; the first matching condition wins. Pick a condition and type its value, or use the suggestion for the network you're on. "This network" matches a specific router by its gateway MAC (precise; tells apart networks that share a subnet); "subnet" matches an IP range. Add separate rules to connect and to disconnect. An "otherwise" rule fires when none of the rules above it match — keep it last as the fallback, usually with the opposite action.
automation.empty: No rules — this tunnel is never auto-managed. Add a rule below.
automation.cond_none_desc: matches when no rule above matched — keep it last as the fallback
automation.ssid_select_hint: Select or enter a Wi-Fi name
automation.drag_hint: drag to reorder — the topmost matching rule wins
automation.mac_invalid: not a valid MAC address (e.g. b0:38:6c:54:8b:ab)
